Resolves #20106

A list's record-change handler now re-renders the changed record at the record's current index. `Neo.list.Base#onStoreRecordChange` and `Neo.list.Buffered#onStoreRecordChange` read `store.indexOf(record)` instead of the payload's `data.index`, which `Store#onRecordChange` takes before any listener runs. When a listener registered ahead of the list re-sorted the Store on the same edit, the stale index wrote the record's item into another record's slot. The Fleet roster's controller does exactly that on every `state` change. The result was a duplicate `li` in the vdom and a removed one on the page. If the record returned inside one 500 ms transition, its real node stayed at another card's position for good: the vnode was correct and the DOM was stale. That is the roster's empty slot with one card stacked on another, from the operator's 10-24 and 10-25 screenshots.

Evidence: L3 (component tier in a real browser comparing the settled DOM to the vnode, plus a live Neural Link read of the installed Fleet Manager with the same signature) → L3 required (AC-1 compares the DOM to the vnode). Residual: none.

## Deltas from ticket

None substantive. `menu/List#onSourceStoreRecordChange` keeps its own `indexOf` resolution, now redundant, as the ticket's Out of Scope says.

## Test Evidence

All coverage runs in CI. The one outside-CI receipt is the live read on the operator's Fleet Manager (Neural Link, 2026-10-25 15:2xZ). The vdom and vnode both held Maryam's `li` at index 3 with `translate(10px, 133px)`, while the DOM held it at index 8 with `translate(10px, 379px)`, which is Vega's slot. The component spec reproduces that state.
